issue_context.title: networkd support for advmss setting on routes
issue_context.body:
Please consider adding support for the "advmss" option on routing table entries configured via systemd.network? This option is used to workaround issues with Path-MTU discovery (which can often result from blocked ICMP messages). FYI The "advmss" option is able to be configured on routes added using the "ip route" command, so I'd like equivalent functionality to be available in systemd-networkd? (Please see "man ip-route" for more information on the "advmss" setting?)

My use case for this setting is due to a combination of factors:
- The connection to my ISP uses PPPoE protocol which in practical terms reduces the packet size that I can send to or receive from the Internet by 8 bytes, to 1492 bytes.
- My ISP performs MSS clamping to reduce the Maximal Segment Size used for TCP connections by 8 bytes, to 1452, however there is a bug in the implementation which means that it doesn't get set in the SYN/ACK response to incoming TCP connections (to me).
- An Internet-based client connecting to my server will therefore think the MSS is 1460 bytes, and so will likely try to send packets that are too big to reach me. In that circumstance, my ISP will reply with ICMP Destination Unreachable (The datagram is too big), and the expectation is that the client will adjust their MSS and retransmit the data in smaller packets.
- However, if the client doesn't receive the ICMP messages because they are behind a firewall which drops all ICMP messages, then they will continue trying to retransmit the original packet size, and the TCP connection will stall (and eventually time out).

The workaround that I had been using (prior to using systemd-networkd) was to set the "advmss" option on my server's default route, so the server will send the correct MSS value (1452) to any client connecting from the Internet.

Without this option the alternatives that I have considered are:
- Use networkd-dispatcher to add routes using "ip route" with the desired advmss setting. This is quite a clumsy way of adding network routes.
- Set an artificially low MTU on the network interface, resulting in the desired MSS value being calculated for all TCP connections using that interface. However that MSS is used for all connections, rather than being tied to a particular routing table entry. (FYI This is the option I am currently using.)

Ideally I'd like the ability to configure a route with advmss option along the following lines:

[Route]
Destination=0.0.0.0/0
Gateway=192.168.20.1
AdvMSS=1452

Thanks very much,
Nick.

review_comments:
so, we should filter out "0" here, and refuse it.

Our usual way how to unset an option is by assigning the empty string to it. Hence, please:

1. refuse TCPAdvertisedMaximumSegmentSize=0 here
2. support TCPAdvertisedMaximumSegmentSize= and in that case set the field to 0

i.e. implicit behaviour of some magic undocumented special values is not OK. We should make this explicit, i.e. empty string should universally mean "unset" or "reset to defaults". And if you specify a numeric value, then the it should be taken literally, and if that makes no sense (like in this case afaics if zero) be refused.
